messages:
kevin: Quick q — should we standardize on proto-first internal APIs or keep REST everywhere? This affects routing policy, quota propagation, and Console rollout UX. Browser clients + canaries make it messy. anyone?

maria: Proto-first wins for strong contracts, auto-generated clients, and smaller wire payloads. It also makes schema evolution more disciplined. downside: browser support (need grpc-web + envoy) and slightly steeper onboarding.

alex: Rest-first keeps the surface approachable for product teams and external integrators. Easier to debug in Console and curl. But i worry we lose contract guarantees and introduce fragmentation across services.

jia: From a quotas/telemetry angle: gateway translation is fine only if we preserve billing/claim metadata. If we convert proto->json we need a deterministic mapping for token-estimate hints and route claims or our chargeback will be wrong.

sam: Could we normalize token/accounting hints at the gateway boundary? e.g., gateway computes x-token-estimate and x-quota-claim and forwards those into our infra. That keeps downstream agnostic of transport.

oliver: Proposal: hybrid model. Proto-first inside infra. Gateway exposes a thin REST/JSON façade for external apps. Use capability negotiation: clients send `Accept: application/grpc-web` or fallback to JSON. Gateway maintains translation but must inject stable headers: `x-tenant-id`, `x-route-id`, `x-quota-claim`.

kevin: @oliver that sounds promising. How do we keep streaming behavior consistent? incremental token streaming and backpressure are important for chat flows.

maria: grpc has better streaming/backpressure semantics. grpc-web supports chunked responses but there are browser edge cases (older Safari). For streaming we should prefer direct grpc paths from internal services and let the gateway do SSE for browsers.

alex: For Console and dev UX we also need human-readable request/response preview. When gateway translates proto->json, expose a preview pane that shows both canonical proto and translated JSON. That helps debug contract mismatches.

jia: Telemetry plan: tag traces with `route_id`, `transport` (grpc|grpc-web|http-json), `gateway_version` and `translation_hash`. Emit `x-proto-schema-version` header from services so we can correlate schema drift. Also include `x-translation-duration-ms` for the gateway.

sam: Migration plan idea: 1) proto-first for internal runtimes only, gateway accepts both transports. 2) run both for 30–90 days. 3) canary rules: start 1% grpc traffic to new path, observe p99 latency, 5xx, and quota burn anomalies. 4) promote when signals are green. Console should show rollout toggle + rollback button.

oliver: Example header mapping sketch (gateway transforms):
```
# gateway inbound -> internal service
x-tenant-id: {{tenant.id}}
x-route-id: {{route.id}}
x-quota-claim: service:tokens:estimated={{estimated_tokens}}
# gateway adds translation metadata
x-translation-hash: {{sha256(proto->json map)}}
x-translation-duration-ms: {{ms}}
```

oliver: And a tiny Envoy route fragment we tested: 
```
- match: { path: /v1/chat }
  route: { cluster: chat-internal }
  request_headers_to_add:
    - header: { key: x-transport, value: grpc-web }
    - header: { key: x-route-id, value: chat.v1 }
```

maria: Schema evolution rule: use reserved field numbers, avoid repurposing. For optional features, prefer `oneof` or explicit feature flags in the proto. Keep server-side defaults immutable in a major version.

alex: On the Console side we will need a new view: "Transport & Translation" for each route showing: accepted transports, translation rules, header injections, and a live sample transforming proto<->json. Also surface canary health signals per-transport.

jia: Ops/alerting: create alerts for translation errors (JSON->proto rejects), token-estimate variance > 15%, and sudden shifts in `transport` distribution. Those usually indicate client regressions.

sam: Ops question — how do we handle client libs? We can generate JS/TS clients from proto and publish a lightweight npm package that falls back to REST for browsers without grpc-web. That way product teams get typed clients by default.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for `grpc-gateway-v2` -> 1% of traffic to eastus-capacity. Link: https://deploys.internal/release/3291 :rocket:

kevin: OK action items: (1) oliver/maria prototype gateway header mapping + translation for chat.v1 (2) devex (alex) draft Console mock for Transport & Translation view (3) jia set up telemetry keys and alerts (4) sam write canary signal checklist.

maria: I'll spike grpc-web edge cases (Safari, mobile web).

alex: I'll mock the Console pane by EOD Friday, will include sample proto<->json diff view.

oliver: Starting a branch with Envoy config + translation lambda. Will post PR link when ready.

kevin: sweet. BTW +1 on the hybrid approach. Catch up in tomorrow's architecture sync. :thumbsup:
